The passage is: "For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning. For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them. But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire."

This passage describes the fate of those who have learned about the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, escaped the corruption of the world through this knowledge, but then return to their old ways and are overcome. The passage suggests that it would have been better for them to not have known the way of righteousness at all, than to turn away from it after knowing it. The passage compares such individuals to a dog that returns to its vomit or a sow that, after being washed, returns to wallowing in the mud. It is a warning against turning away from the teachings of Christ after having learned them.
